paper.title: Electronic excited states in deep variational Monte Carlo
paper.authors: Mike Entwistle, Zeno Schätzle, Paolo A. Erdman, Jan Hermann, Frank Noé

results.system_description: Li atom, all electrons, clamped point nucleus, 2 up and 1 down electrons
results.variant: PauliNet, ground state of the penalty-method run
results.source_location: Supplementary Table II, first row of the atom ('E_n' column)
results.eligibility_evidence: VMC energy of the ground state of the penalty-method calculation; the ground state is optimized by unconstrained energy minimization, the overlap penalty acting only on the excited states (Methods).
results.notes: N_up = 2, N_down = 1: the CASSCF baseline of Supplementary Table VIII has M = 1 for this atom ('M = (N_up - N_down)/2' in the text, but M = 1 for Li and B can only be N_up - N_down), and PauliNet keeps the S_z of its baseline. The C, N and O rows of the same table are in the sectors with M = 0, 1 and 0 (low M_S), other instances than the high-spin sectors, and are recorded on those (decision P6, 2026-11-02).

results.system_description: C atom, all electrons, clamped point nucleus, 3 up and 3 down electrons
results.variant: PauliNet, ground state of the penalty-method run
results.source_location: Supplementary Table II (table:small_atoms), first row of the atom ('E_n' column)
results.eligibility_evidence: VMC energy of the ground state of the penalty-method calculation; the ground state is optimized by unconstrained energy minimization, the overlap penalty acting only on the excited states (Methods).
results.notes: N_up = 3, N_down = 3: the CASSCF baseline of Supplementary Table VIII has M = 0 for C, and PauliNet keeps the S_z of its baseline ('Spin treatment', Methods). This is the M_S = 0 sector of the 3P ground term, below its maximal M_S = 1 (decision P6, 2026-11-02): the exact energy is that of the ground term, the variational problem is another instance than mol-c-isolated-atom-s2.

results.system_description: N atom, all electrons, clamped point nucleus, 4 up and 3 down electrons
results.variant: PauliNet, ground state of the penalty-method run
results.source_location: Supplementary Table II (table:small_atoms), first row of the atom ('E_n' column)
results.eligibility_evidence: VMC energy of the ground state of the penalty-method calculation; the ground state is optimized by unconstrained energy minimization, the overlap penalty acting only on the excited states (Methods).
results.notes: N_up = 4, N_down = 3: the CASSCF baseline of Supplementary Table VIII has M = 1 for N, which for an odd number of electrons can only be N_up - N_down = 1, as for Li and B; PauliNet keeps the S_z of its baseline ('Spin treatment', Methods). This is the M_S = 1/2 sector of the 4S ground term, below its maximal M_S = 3/2 (decision P6, 2026-11-02); another instance than mol-n-isolated-atom-s3.

results.system_description: Ethene at the geometry 'Barbatti torsion 0 deg', all electrons, 8 up and 8 down electrons, clamped nuclei
results.variant: PauliNet, ground state of the penalty-method run
results.source_location: Supplementary Table V (table:ethylene), tau = 0 deg (phi = 0), first row ('E_n')
results.eligibility_evidence: VMC energy of the ground state of the penalty-method calculation; the ground state is optimized by unconstrained energy minimization, the overlap penalty acting only on the excited states (Methods).
results.notes: Geometry: the planar ethylene of Barbatti, Paier and Lischka (2004), printed in arXiv:2203.09472v3 Supplementary Table I, with the torsion angle tau varied 'while keeping all other geometric parameters fixed' (2203.09472v3, Results): the CH2 group on the +x carbon is rotated rigidly about the C-C axis, as in the code release of Pfau et al. (google-deepmind/ferminet, ferminet/configs/excited/twisted_ethylene.py) and the parametrized table of arXiv:2503.19847v2 (tab:ethylen_geom); coordinates rounded to 1e-6 angstrom. Singlet, N_up = N_down = 8. The CASSCF baseline is a singlet (Supplementary Table VIII, C2H4: M = 0), and for ethylene the spin state is held by the frozen determinant coefficients ('Spin treatment', Methods). The pyramidalization rows of the same table (phi at tau = 90 deg) are another geometry family and are not recorded.
